title: Result Instead of throws
hints: `Result<Success, Failure>` stores success or failure as a value.
Return `.failure(...)` for each bad case; switch on the result to build each line; `get()` turns it back into throwing style.
jsBridge: `Result<Success, Failure>` is a typed either, like returning `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false, error }` in TS. It was vital for callback APIs before async/await. Now it's mostly used to store outcomes, since `throws` covers control flow.
